headline: Ex-Jamalpur MP Noor Mohammed arrested in Dhaka’s Gulshan

caption:
Former Jamalpur-1 MP Nur Mohammed has been arrested in Dhaka’s Gulshan in connection with the 2024 July Uprising.

Former Jamalpur-1 member of parliament Nur Mohammed was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) on Saturday evening.

The arrest took place at a house in Dhaka’s Gulshan, which the former MP claimed is his own property, according to DB chief Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam.

Nur Mohammed is accused in several cases relating to the 2024 July Uprising and has been brought to the DB offices for questioning.

The former lawmaker, who was elected in the January 2024 polls, will be taken to court on Sunday as the cases are being scrutinised.

Beyond his parliamentary role, Nur Mohammed served as the president of Bakshiganj Upazila Awami League and as the treasurer of the district’s Awami League unit.

headline_marked: Bills for [[anti-drug tribunals and firearm use]] introduced in Parliament
headline: Bills for anti-drug tribunals and firearm use introduced in Parliament
summary: The Narcotics Control (Amendment) Bill 2026 proposes separate tribunals for faster drug crime trials, dog squads, and allowing narcotics officers to carry firearms.
details: The Narcotics Control (Amendment) Bill, 2026, has been introduced in parliament to speed up the trials of drug-related crimes through the formation of separate tribunals.
The proposed law would designate the Department of Narcotics Control as a specialized organization with uniformed and firearm-equipped manpower, allowing its members to use firearms.
Further proposals include the creation of a dog squad, a separate jail for the department, a cybercrime control wing, a digital forensic lab, and a money laundering prevention cell.
Simultaneously, the Cyber Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was introduced to abolish the crime and punishment clause for gambling in cyberspace from the Cyber Security Act.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the narcotics bill, while Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Faqir Mahbub Anam introduced the cyber security bill.
Both bills have been sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs for scrutiny and a report to be delivered within three meeting days.
During the session, the Leader of the Opposition, Shafiqur Rahman, raised concerns regarding the procedural adherence before the bills were raised in the house.
caption:
Separate tribunals, dog squads, and firearms for narcotics officers? Two major amendment bills hit Parliament.

The Narcotics Control (Amendment) Bill, 2026, has been introduced in parliament to speed up the trials of drug-related crimes through the formation of separate tribunals.

The proposed law would designate the Department of Narcotics Control as a specialized organization with uniformed and firearm-equipped manpower, allowing its members to use firearms.

Further proposals include the creation of a dog squad, a separate jail for the department, a cybercrime control wing, a digital forensic lab, and a money laundering prevention cell.

Simultaneously, the Cyber Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was introduced to abolish the crime and punishment clause for gambling in cyberspace from the Cyber Security Act.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the narcotics bill, while Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Faqir Mahbub Anam introduced the cyber security bill.

Both bills have been sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs for scrutiny and a report to be delivered within three meeting days.

During the session, the Leader of the Opposition, Shafiqur Rahman, raised concerns regarding the procedural adherence before the bills were raised in the house.
